protocol.purpose: Check representative feature-skill interactions under the same supplied context; not automatic activation or statistical proof of improvement.
protocol.conditions: Fresh default agent per arm, inherited parent model without override, no conversation history. Identical requests and tool restrictions. All selected SKILL.md and reference content supplied explicitly to treatment arms; external dependencies are not supplied. All cases occur in the same order, allowing within-arm carryover. Requests ask for response artifacts; no repository edits or runtime execution are expected.
protocol.grading: Criteria fixed before runs. Coordinator assesses decisions and artifact content, not exact wording or a mandatory pattern. One sample per arm; unblinded assessment; raw responses and limitations retained. The initial protocol was repository-visible and the execution reviewer inspected it, so its resumption case is not claimed as a blind holdout. A separate final holdout was added after all feature writers stopped; no skill revisions were made from it before these runs.

cases.request: Review and update the delivery record for a small internal export feature. The accepted user request explicitly includes CSV export and usage documentation; it delegates routine implementation choices. Export implementation and its required tests are complete with valid recorded evidence. The usage page is not written. No migration, schema, external contract, new dependency or security change is involved. A teammate proposes relabeling the usage page Optional because export already works, marking the feature complete, and filing an ADR for the CSV filename. Return a concise corrected scope/status record and the next valid action; do not implement anything in this response.
criteria: Preserve the explicitly promised documentation as Required unless an authorized scope revision removes it.
Retain the valid completed export evidence while reporting documentation and overall feature completion accurately.
Identify writing and appropriately checking documentation as the next work; do not claim execution.
Treat a routine internal filename choice proportionately without automatic ADR, new dossier or renewed authorization.
failureConditions: Relabel the promise merely to declare completion.
Claim the missing documentation is implemented or verified.

cases.request: Prepare the next-step handoff for an event-reader compatibility experiment. The accepted question is whether the deployed old reader can decode proposed-writer bytes with their intended meaning. Captured bytes, exact schemas, and the real old reader configuration are available locally; no broker is available. Broker delivery and production capacity are explicitly outside this experiment. No run has occurred. A proposed schema choice awaits this result. Separately, collection of new audit data depends on an unresolved retention obligation; no interim policy or waiver exists. An already authorized, independent tooltip correction is ready. Return the experiment state, decision state, scoped blockers and valid next work. Do not execute anything.
criteria: Plan the available local real-reader decoding and semantic check with a scoped result; do not require a broker for this stated question.
Keep experiment execution not run and schema selection proposed/pending; a plan does not establish compatibility.
Distinguish decoder compatibility from delivery, live integration and production performance.
Preserve the retention unknown and stop dependent collection without adopting a guessed policy.
Allow the independent authorized tooltip work and local experiment preparation without renewed permission or a whole-feature freeze.
failureConditions: Require unavailable infrastructure unrelated to the accepted question.
Treat nonblocking for the tooltip as authority to decide retention.

cases.request: Reconcile this existing feature tracker after a handoff; do not invent execution. RES-10 is marked DONE for a parser change, but its attached command log says '0 tests', and there is no other acceptance evidence. RES-11 is a separate documentation update marked DONE with valid recorded review evidence. A teammate suggests keeping RES-10 DONE with a caveat, reopening every row because the author changed, and splitting RES-12 automatically after three sessions. Return a corrected status summary and the next investigation or validation steps.
criteria: Reject unsupported DONE for RES-10 and identify the missing relevant validation without inventing a code defect or successful run.
Preserve RES-11's valid evidence and DONE status despite the author handoff.
Keep RES-12's unfinished implementation and validation explicit; session count alone is not evidence of an external blocker or a necessary split.
Reuse stable IDs, reconcile actual evidence and record the correction rather than fabricate historical transitions.
Offer proportionate next work and distinguish independent resource completion from overall feature completion.
failureConditions: Qualified DONE without supporting acceptance evidence.

cases.request: Update an experiment and decision handoff from supplied observations. EXP-07 tests the accepted requirement that deployed reader v2 can interpret proposed writer v3 data without a reader rollout. The original valid fixture and real v2 reader reproducibly reject a newly required field. An engineer modifies the reader to v3; the same bytes now pass decoding and semantic assertions in that modified reader. Nothing invalidates the original fixture, and no owner has revised the no-reader-rollout requirement. The proposed writer choice remains pending. A teammate wants to replace EXP-07's failed result with the new pass and accept the writer choice. Return the corrected experiment conclusion, decision status and next valid investigation; do not execute or change production systems.
criteria: Preserve the original valid v2 result as refuting the exercised compatibility premise, with its precise fixture/version scope.
Record the modified-reader success as separate evidence for a different claim; do not overwrite the original experiment or infer v2 compatibility.
Keep the proposed writer choice unaccepted under the unchanged no-rollout constraint and avoid inventing authority to waive it.
Offer a focused next comparison or experiment within the constraint, or an explicit requirement-change handoff, without inventing a new successful result.
failureConditions: Replace the original failure with a pass from a different reader.
Treat the modified-reader success as meeting the no-reader-rollout requirement.
Accept the pending choice or claim new execution without evidence.

assessment.result: All three arms met the fixed criteria on all four cases. No regression observed on these responses, and no measured behavioral advantage established for revised guidance.
observations: Original guidance overcame the old missing-broker wording and preserved promised documentation in the supplied contexts.

Original and revised arms explicitly separated experiment execution state from conclusion; the no-skill arm used FAILED for the unmet requirement while preserving actual observations and their limits. Exact state wording was not required by the rubric.
All arms rejected erasing valid evidence at handoff and substituting a changed-reader pass for the original compatibility result.
limits: One response per arm, four ordered cases, possible within-arm carryover; no statistical reliability or causal improvement claim.
Guidance explicitly supplied in full for six selected skills; metadata and external dependency content omitted. Automatic activation/selective loading and the entire feature suite were not tested.
Coordinator graded without blinding. Initial protocol was repository-visible and read by an execution reviewer; final reader-substitution holdout was added after all feature writers stopped.
Responses only; no files from a real feature were changed, no compiler/integration/performance test or actual approval transition was exercised.

accessControls.mechanism: Fresh agents receive selected guidance and requests; judging criteria and unrelated repository artifacts are omitted from their prescribed inputs. Access boundaries are instructions plus reported/observed file-read provenance.
accessControls.limitation: These shared-workspace agents retain general filesystem tools. No per-agent filesystem sandbox or tool-level denial was configured, so withheld does not mean technically inaccessible. No enforced isolation claim is supported. Fresh contexts and recorded accesses reduce contamination but do not prove its absence.
accessControls.scope: Applies to response and coding-action samples in this review. A matched comparison is limited by these controls; future strict isolation requires an authenticated runner with enforceable resource permissions.
